headline: No planner configuration is shown to clear both gates: the {count.passing.pass_rate|words} that pass in every task both overrun the {criteria.p95.threshold} latency budget.
lede: Brisk-S high reasoning with retry, the cheaper of those two, has a tail latency of {measure.latency_ms.brisk-s.high.r1.p95} over all cases. Two things could change the answer: per-task latency, which the budget reads and nobody recorded, and per-task pass rates at the line, where both Brisk-S setups with retry sit within margins a fresh run could reverse.

caveats.label: Per-task pass rates state no count
caveats.material_if: Material wherever a gate reading sits near the line: Brisk-S low reasoning with retry, inside the budget over all cases, misses ambiguous-entity asks by {criteria.pass_rate.brisk-s.low.r1.disamb.gap|abs} points, a miss a run of today's size would read as a pass {assumed.share.settle.criteria.pass_rate.brisk-s.low.r1.task.disamb.wrong_side} of the time, so it could yet clear both gates.

caveats.label: Latency not recorded per task
caveats.material_if: Only if the tasks do not split the cases between them: the reading that some task overruns the budget rests on an overall tail over it, and the budget itself is read in each task.

Only if Brisk-S high reasoning with retry is taken forward on its multi-hop clearance of {assumed.share.settle.criteria.pass_rate.brisk-s.high.r1.task.multihop.distance} points: as the best of {n_candidates}, a fresh run tends to read it lower.
Only for comparisons between configurations, which read unpaired and so wider than they would paired; each gate reading stands against its own line.

decision.text: On point estimates, only Atlas-M and Brisk-S, each with high reasoning and one retry, clear the pass-rate gate in all four tasks. Both overrun the latency budget over all cases, and Atlas-M costs {cost_per_month.atlas-m.high.r1} a month against Brisk-S's {cost_per_month.brisk-s.high.r1}.

Reasoning effort buys the pass rate and spends the latency budget: every configuration inside the budget overall misses the pass-rate gate in at least one task, and the latency gate itself has no figure in any task.

Brisk-S high reasoning with retry clears each task by a point and a half or less. Reading each task as holding its traffic share of cases, a run of today's size would read it below the line on multi-hop {assumed.share.settle.criteria.pass_rate.brisk-s.high.r1.task.multihop.wrong_side} of the time, on ambiguous entity {assumed.share.settle.criteria.pass_rate.brisk-s.high.r1.task.disamb.wrong_side} and on date math {assumed.share.settle.criteria.pass_rate.brisk-s.high.r1.task.datemath.wrong_side}.

Brisk-S low reasoning with retry sits exactly on the line in date math, so a run reads it either side {assumed.share.settle.criteria.pass_rate.brisk-s.low.r1.task.datemath.wrong_side} of the time; the routed mix in the next steps leans on this leg and on the three thin legs above.

Tail latency per task and case-counted reruns of the legs at the line for the two Brisk-S setups with retry, then a measured run of the routed mix; failing that, the planner owner declares which line gives.

claims.text: On point estimates, only {count.passing.pass_rate|words} of {n_candidates} configurations clear the pass-rate gate in every task, both with high reasoning and one retry; several others sit within a point of the line.

evidence.caption: Pass rate by task for the six configurations nearest the gate of {criteria.pass_rate.threshold} in each task; per-task figures state no count, so none carries an interval.

claims.text: Both overrun the latency budget over all cases; only Brisk-S with reasoning off or low, and every Nano-XS setup, stay inside it.

evidence.caption: Median to tail latency over all cases; the budget applies in each task, and the campaign recorded no latency figure for any task.

claims.text: Inside the budget over all cases, the nearest miss is Brisk-S low reasoning with retry: short of the line on multi-hop and ambiguous-entity asks and exactly on it for date math, the tasks high reasoning lifts most.

evidence.caption: Brisk-S low reasoning with retry by task against the gate of {criteria.pass_rate.threshold}; its tail of {measure.latency_ms.brisk-s.low.r1.p95} is over all cases and does not show it inside the budget in each task.

Brisk-S high reasoning minus low reasoning, both with retry, in points; only the overall row has an interval ({compare.brisk-s.high.r1.brisk-s.low.r1.pass_rate.overall.interval}), and it does not exclude zero.

claims.text: The kept failures of Brisk-S low reasoning with retry are planning errors: two hops collapsed into one query, a date window off by a day, and an ambiguous name answered without asking.

evidence.caption: Three kept failures, one each from multi-hop, date math and ambiguous-entity asks; the snapshot keeps a sample, not every failure.

claims.text: One retry lifts Brisk-S's pass rate at both low and high reasoning, and it is what carries high reasoning over the line in the three tasks it otherwise misses.

evidence.caption: Each Brisk-S setting moved alone, in points of overall pass rate; the lift from retry reads smaller at high reasoning, but the interaction is not separated, and the last two rows are that one interaction read from each side.

explore.outcome: No budget value yields a pick as measured: the budget is read in each task and no task has a latency figure, so every configuration stays out or undecided at any line.

explore.binds: Which configurations pass on quality in each task
explore.outcome: Lowering it admits more configurations on pass rate, but none becomes a pick while the latency gate has no per-task figure.

method.text: {n_candidates} configurations crossing three models, three reasoning levels and retry on or off; no control, so every comparison is between two configurations' own figures.
{scoreboard.brisk-s.high.r1.cases} cases per configuration, none lost, spread over four tasks by traffic share; per-task figures state no case count.
The campaign does not state its pass rule; the kept failures are scored against an expected call plan and classed as a missing call, wrong arguments or the wrong tool.
Pass rate at least {criteria.pass_rate.threshold} and tail latency at most {criteria.p95.threshold}, each read in every task on the point estimate.

The p95 latency, recorded only over all cases; the budget is declared per task, so it is read as unknown in each task, with an overall figure over the budget implying some task is over it too. Where the full gate grid marks a latency cell as failing with no figure, read it as unknown.

Overall pass-rate differences carry a binomial interval computed from case counts, at the level each table prints, combined unpaired, which errs wide where configurations ran the same cases. How often a rerun reads the other way, and the cases it needs, read each task as holding its traffic share of cases, an assumption; sizes are two-sided.
